newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian pilots to tighten vigilance over India.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian pilots to tighten vigilance over India.

text.p: Malaysian pilots flying into India have run into communication problems in the past and will be more vigilant in India following Tuesday's mid-air collision, a Malaysian pilots group president said on Wednesday.

The chief of the Malaysian Airlines Pilots Association said pilots have sometimes experienced communications problems over the Bay of Bengal but not so much around the Indian capital of New Delhi, the site of Tuesday's collision.
"Flying to India we have experienced communications problems on the radio, especially over the Bay of Bengal," Captain Mohamad Nawawi said.
"Madras (air traffic control) covers three quarters of the Bay of Bengal region. We can sometimes hardly (hear) them," Nawawi said.

But he said communications close to New Delhi's international airport were better, noting that its control tower operated on a high frequency radio band. He added, however, that air traffic there has risen steadily in recent years.
He said Malaysian pilots would be more vigilant about flying to India after the crash.
An Ilyushin Il-76 freighter from the former Soviet republic of Kazakhstan collided with a Saudi Arabian Airlines Boeing 747 passenger jet on Tuesday in the world's worst mid-air crash.
